question: Should you buy DLF Limited at ₹785.00 today, wait for a support pullback, or deploy capital elsewhere?

epigraph.quote: Own the finest land and rental assets in a cycle, but insist on buying them when the tape offers margin of safety rather than euphoria.

web_blocks.title: Dual Verdict: Strong Stage 2 Franchise, REJECTED on Valuation

web_blocks.html: DLF Limited (NSE: DLF) is India's top luxury home builder and Grade-A office landlord [6]. As of September 2026, it holds ₹15,084 crore in cash against ₹314 crore in debt, though ₹12,270 crore sits in RERA escrow [6]. It also owns a 188 msf legacy land bank and a 66.67% stake in the 50 msf AAA-rated DCCDL rental platform [6]. Under Ind AS 115 rules, ₹60,134 crore of sold homes with ₹28,700 crore of future gross margin sit off the P&L awaiting occupation certificates [6, 13]. Yet 72% of land potential and 84% of recent sales sit in Gurugram/NCR [9]. H1FY27 pre-sales also fell 72% YoY to ₹4,460 crore against ₹20,000 crore full-year guidance [6, 18]. This earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality verdict and a PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI grade [6, 9, 18].

On November 20, 2026, DLF closed at ₹785.00 (₹1,93,940.66 crore market cap; 42.55x TTM P/E; 4.26x P/B) [23]. Stage 2 momentum is strong, with shares +14.40% above the 50-day SMA (₹686.16) and Daily RSI(14) at 73.74 on 1.71x volume [23, 24]. However, our un-double-counted SOTP is ₹820.00/sh (+4.5% vs CMP; EV ₹808.00) [6, 9]. Even at the ₹748.54 support top against a ₹644.85 stop, asymmetry is 0.69:1—below our 1.50:1 gate [24]. Under the Anti-Hedging Rule, we assign REJECTED on VALUATION (TIER_0; cash equity only, as DLF is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), revisiting only below ₹650 or if H2FY27 bookings and OCF prove a higher SOTP [24, 26].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to this institutional monograph on DLF Limited, India's largest listed real estate developer and commercial landlord. Before we dive into eighty years of corporate history, Gurugram land economics, and ten-year financial forensics, let us start at the finish line with a clear executive summary of what DLF is worth, how its chart looks, and what you should actually do with your money.

As of November 20, 2026, DLF shares closed at ₹785.00, valuing the company at ₹1,93,941 crore. On the surface, the stock looks expensive at 42.55 times trailing earnings and 4.26 times book value. Underneath that surface, however, DLF is a far stronger business than its reported income statement suggests. After surviving a brutal post-2008 debt trap by partnering with Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC, DLF now holds ₹15,084 crore in cash against just ₹314 crore of parent borrowings.

At the same time, DLF owns two-thirds of DCCDL, a triple-A rated commercial rental empire spanning fifty million square feet of prime offices and malls at ninety-six percent occupancy. That rental business is on track for ₹7,550 crore of exit annual rent in fiscal 2027 and ₹10,000 crore over the medium term. Meanwhile, Indian accounting rules force DLF to wait until apartments are handed over before booking residential sales as revenue—leaving ₹60,134 crore of already-sold luxury homes and ₹28,700 crore of embedded profit waiting in the pipeline.

Why, then, do we classify DLF's business quality as CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL rather than an unconditional compounder? Two honest reasons stand out. First, seventy-two percent of DLF's 188-million-square-foot land bank and eighty-four percent of its recent sales are concentrated inside one market: Gurugram and the National Capital Region. Second, residential pre-sales are inherently lumpy—bookings fell seventy-two percent year-over-year in the first half of fiscal 2027 to ₹4,460 crore, leaving a steep climb to meet management's ₹20,000 crore full-year target. In addition, eighty-one percent of DLF's headline cash pile sits inside project-specific RERA escrow accounts.

book_subsections.title: Our Dual Verdict: Great Franchise, REJECTED on Valuation Today
paragraphs: When we combine fundamental valuation with technical tape analysis, our verdict is clear: REJECTED on VALUATION, with a Tier 0 rating. DLF's Stage 2 momentum is genuinely strong, sitting 14.40 percent above its fifty-day moving average of ₹686.16 with a daily RSI(14) of 73.74. Yet our un-double-counted Sum-of-the-Parts valuation puts fair value at ₹820.00 per share—just 4.5 percent above today's ₹785.00 close.

Even if you wait for a routine pullback to ₹748.54 around the twenty-day average at ₹726.71 and the ten-week exponential line at ₹711.15, your upside to ₹820.00 is only 9.5 percent against ₹103.69 of risk to the ₹644.85 stop. That yields a 0.69-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio, failing our 1.50-to-1 gate. Across our twelve-month scenarios—₹980.00 bull at twenty-five percent odds, ₹820.00 base at fifty-five percent odds, and ₹560.00 bear at twenty percent odds—the probability-weighted value is ₹808.00. DLF would only become interesting on a deeper reset below ₹650 or if second-half bookings and operating cash flow prove a higher SOTP.

book_subsections.title: How to Execute With Zero FOMO
paragraphs: Because DLF is currently NOT_HELD in your Zerodha portfolio and has no liquid listed options chain, your execution plan is simple. First, pass on DLF at ₹785.00 and keep sixty percent of this capital budget in cash as dry powder for a deeper reset below ₹650. Second, put the remaining forty percent to work immediately in shortlisted pharma compounder Zydus Lifesciences at ₹1,200.00, which offers a 2.62-to-1 asymmetry ratio toward ₹1,420.00 without technical overextension. Third, keep Mumbai developer Lodha on your watchlist at ₹1,218.70 as a lower-multiple backup. Let us now walk through the full story from Chapter 1 onward.

book_subsections.title: How This Monograph Is Organized for You
paragraphs: Chapters 1 through 6 examine DLF completely blind to today's share price. We trace how Chaudhary Raghvendra Singh founded the firm in 1946, how the 2008 debt crisis nearly broke it, and how the 2017 GIC joint venture rebuilt the balance sheet. We break down every business line—luxury residential homes, DCCDL offices, and retail malls—using concrete projects like The Camellias, The Arbour, Privana, and The Dahlias.

We also audit DLF's competitive moat against Lodha, Godrej Properties, Prestige Estates, and Oberoi Realty, test management's promises against actual delivery, and unpack the five accounting quirks—especially Ind AS 115 revenue lag and RERA escrow rules—that confuse most investors.

Then, in Chapters 7 through 9, we bring in the live November 20, 2026 market price of ₹785.00. We run an un-double-counted Sum-of-the-Parts valuation and Reverse DCF, inspect the weekly, daily, and four-hour price charts, debate the strongest bull and bear arguments, and lay out our scenario math and capital redeployment plan.

As you listen or read through the chapters ahead, keep four anchor numbers in mind. First is ₹60,134 crore—the backlog of already-sold homes waiting to be recognised as revenue under Ind AS 115. Second is ₹12,270 crore—the portion of DLF's ₹15,084 crore cash pile that is legally locked inside RERA project escrow accounts. Third is ₹820.00 per share—our un-double-counted base-case SOTP fair value. Fourth is ₹650.00—the deeper valuation reset level below which DLF would become interesting again.

Keep those four numbers handy, and every detail in this monograph will snap into focus. Whether you keep sixty percent in cash or deploy forty percent into Zydus Lifesciences today, you will be making an informed, unemotional decision backed by primary filings and strict risk math.

Above all, remember that passing on an extended ₹785.00 entry is not pessimism—it is price discipline. DLF is a survivor with irreplaceable Gurugram land and a growing triple-A rental engine. Under our Anti-Hedging Rule, we simply refuse to pay peak momentum prices or hedge with a watch verdict when even a support pullback offers only 0.69-to-1 reward-to-risk.

book_callouts.title: Executive Bottom Line
book_callouts.text: DLF is a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL Stage 2 leader with a fortress balance sheet, but our ₹820.00 SOTP leaves 0.69:1 support asymmetry (< 1.50:1 gate), triggering REJECTED on VALUATION (TIER_0). Revisit only below ₹650 or on proven H2FY27 bookings + OCF.
